candidates.source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — CDX Server API (host-scoped snapshot enumeration for ME vendor/bank domains)
candidates.why_relevant: Only durable mechanism to recover deleted vendor reference/case-study pages and dead bank product pages (.me and regional vendor domains). Lets you enumerate every captured URL path for a host and diff over time, which surfaces 'reference/klijenti/rjesenja' pages that vendors removed after contracts ended.
candidates.legal_status: public archive; Terms of Use apply, non-commercial research crawling generally tolerated
candidates.suggested_collection_method: CDX API host queries (url=<vendordomain>/*&collapse=urlkey&filter=statuscode:200) per actor in the ME vendor/bank actor map, then targeted timestamped snapshot fetch of matched paths (reference, klijenti, case, projekti, rjesenja, solutions)
queries_used: web.archive.org Crna Gora banka reference projekat kompanija stara stranica arhiva

candidates.source_name: Wayback Machine snapshot interface (per-URL time travel)
candidates.why_relevant: Retrieves the actual archived HTML of dead vendor case studies, bank e-banking product pages and tender annexes, i.e. the evidence itself rather than a pointer.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch id_-suffixed raw snapshots for URLs returned by CDX; store snapshot timestamp as evidence date
queries_used: web.archive.org Crna Gora banka reference projekat kompanija stara stranica arhiva

candidates.source_name: Službeni list Crne Gore — official gazette registry (registri)
candidates.why_relevant: Primary legal record: publishes CBCG decisions on payment systems (odluke o platnim sistemima, RTGS minimum value, incident reporting), the Zakon o platnom prometu and its amendments, plus government decisions establishing e-government/e-payment bodies. Gazette issue numbers are the durable citation anchor for any regulatory-driven procurement wave.
candidates.access_status: open web; issue-level registry pages (e.g. broj 22/2026 registry GUID URLs)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate issue registry pages, keyword filter on 'platni promet', 'platni sistem', 'informacioni sistem', 'elektronsko plaćanje', 'digitalizacija'; keep issue number + date as citation
queries_used: Službeni list Crne Gore platni promet informacioni sistem odluka

candidates.source_name: Paragraf.me — arhiva službenih glasila (Službeni list CG i opštinski propisi)
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial legal aggregator with a back-archive of gazette issues, including municipal-level acts. Useful fallback when sluzbenilist.me lacks older scans, and municipal acts reveal local e-payment / fiscalisation projects and their contractors.
candidates.legal_status: commercial database; ToS likely restrict bulk scraping
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/low-rate browsing of the arhiva index; treat as lookup, not bulk crawl
queries_used: Službeni list Crne Gore platni promet informacioni sistem odluka

candidates.source_name: PropisiNet.me — Zakon o platnom prometu (consolidated law with amendment history)
candidates.why_relevant: Consolidated text showing the amendment chain (62/2013, 6/2014, 111/2022, 7/2023, 15/2025). Each amendment wave is a leading indicator of bank IT/compliance procurement; the dates scope which archived vendor pages to hunt for.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Single-page fetch; extract amendment gazette numbers as a timeline index
queries_used: Službeni list Crne Gore platni promet informacioni sistem odluka

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Platni promet i platni sistemi: podzakonski akti
candidates.why_relevant: Central bank's own index of secondary legislation on payment systems (nadzor nad platnim sistemima, RTGS thresholds, incident reporting 90/23). Defines the technical obligations banks must buy software to satisfy.

queries_used: Službeni list Crne Gore platni promet informacioni sistem odluka

candidates.source_name: ePlaćanje — national e-payment portal for administrative taxes and fees
candidates.why_relevant: The live front end of the state e-payment scheme (NS NAT). Its card-acceptance chain (acquirer bank, PSP, 3-D Secure provider) is observable from the payment flow and page assets, identifying which payment vendor holds the state account — the reference win competitors will cite.

negative_findings.result_summary: Only 4 of the planned ~12 queries executed (3 sr, 1 mixed). Coverage of the state-digital-counterpart half of the cell is therefore shallower than the archive half.

negative_findings.description: Fetched https://www.gov.me/clanak/sistem-za-elektronsko-placanje in full; it names the system (NS NAT) and the owning ministry but discloses no vendor, integrator, acquirer bank, funding source or dates.
negative_findings.result_summary: State e-payment implementer not identified from the government's own description page.

negative_findings.description: The Strategija digitalne transformacije 2022–2026 PDF (2.2MB, ntpark.me mirror) downloaded successfully but remote text conversion returned unusable output; institutions, budgets and system lists could not be extracted in this pass.

negative_findings.description: The sr query aimed at archived Montenegrin vendor/bank reference pages returned only live institutional pages and a browser extension listing — no specific archived case-study URLs. General web search does not index Wayback snapshot URLs well.
negative_findings.result_summary: Archived vendor case studies must be reached through the CDX API against a pre-built actor/domain list, not through search engines.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets the collection design: build the actor map first (CBCG bank register + CRPS + tender awards), then archive-enumerate each domain.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin national web-archiving programme (an equivalent of a legal-deposit web archive at the Nacionalna biblioteka Crne Gore 'Đurđe Crnojević' or Državni arhiv Crne Gore) was located in this pass; local terms 'nacionalna biblioteka', 'državni arhiv', 'obavezni primjerak' were not searched due to the budget cut-off.
negative_findings.result_summary: Unverified whether a domestic .me web archive exists as an alternative to Wayback.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If one exists it would hold captures Wayback missed for small local vendor sites; if not, Wayback is a single point of failure for this cell.

negative_findings.description: sluzbenilist.me exposes issue-level registry pages via opaque GUID URLs; whether a full-text search endpoint over all issues exists was not established.
negative_findings.result_summary: Systematic keyword retrieval across the gazette is not yet proven feasible.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without full-text search, gazette monitoring degrades to per-issue enumeration, which is far costlier.

coverage_gaps.description: No enumerated list yet of Montenegrin/regional IT and payment vendors serving ME banks, nor their current and historical domains — the prerequisite input for archive enumeration.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the vendor actor map from CRPS name searches, ujn.gov.me award notices and bank annual-report supplier mentions, then run Wayback CDX per domain against paths matching reference|klijenti|projekti|rjesenja|case|solutions.

coverage_gaps.description: Merged/liquidated Montenegrin banks (the richest archive targets) were not enumerated; only the current CBCG register page was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull historical Wayback snapshots of the CBCG Registar banaka page across 2008-2024 to recover names and domains of banks that no longer exist, then archive-crawl each.

coverage_gaps.description: ujn.gov.me was identified but its award/contract notice listings were not opened, so no ME state IT/payment contract award has actually been read in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Open the notice search on ujn.gov.me (and any CEJN public view), filter for IT/software/payment categories, and archive award PDFs immediately since these listings rotate.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell explicitly names the digital-agenda administration, but the current body responsible for state IT operations (successor to MJUDDM functions, e.g. a Uprava/Direktorat for digitalisation and information security) was not located, so its project and contractor pages are uncovered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve the current official name via gov.me organigram, then crawl its projekti / javne nabavke / dokumenta sections and register them as direct sources.

coverage_gaps.description: EU/UNDP/World Bank funded digital projects in ME publish their own tender awards, a channel touched only via one UNDP press release.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add UNDP procurement notices, EU delegation to Montenegro tender pages and TED/EuropeAid award records for ME digital-government lots.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage was met for gazette, strategy and payment terms, but no sr searches were run for archive-specific vocabulary ('arhivirana stranica', 'web arhiva', 'obavezni primjerak', 'Državni arhiv Crne Gore') or for vendor-reference vocabulary ('lista referenci', 'uspješni projekti', 'studija slučaja').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run those sr term sets in a follow-up pass with restored search budget.

brief: For Montenegro, the durable record of vendor wins is split across three channels: the Wayback Machine (the only route to deleted vendor reference/case-study pages and defunct-bank sites, best driven by CDX host enumeration rather than search engines), Službeni list Crne Gore plus CBCG's own payment-system regulation and archive pages (the authoritative, dated legal trail behind each compliance-driven procurement wave), and the state digital-agenda stack — the 2022-2026 Strategija digitalne transformacije, gov.me's document repository, and the NS NAT / ePlaćanje / eKontrola e-payment systems run by the Ministarstvo javne uprave. Critically, the government's own NS NAT page names no implementer, confirming that supplier identity must be recovered from ujn.gov.me procurement awards, CRPS company records and donor (EU/UNDP) tender documents rather than from counterpart communications. The main structural risks are that Wayback is currently an unverified single point of failure (no domestic .me web archive was confirmed) and that the vendor/defunct-bank domain list needed to drive archive enumeration does not yet exist.
